# Torrent Engine fixtures

These fixtures are generated directly with the pinned libtorrent API (2.0.14) and are then
versioned as immutable verification inputs. They are independent of `TorrentEngine::create()`.

`SHA256SUMS` is the machine-checked identity manifest used by the Phase 5 Exit-gate. Run
`sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS` from this directory after any reviewed fixture refresh, and update
the manifest only together with the reviewed replacement bytes and documented expected hashes.

## `create-matrix-*.torrent`

The three files are generated by `generate_create_matrix.cpp` from the same multi-file tree:

- piece length: 16 KiB
- payload root: `payload/`
- `a.bin`: 10,000 bytes, all ASCII `a`
- `nested/b.bin`: 100 bytes, all ASCII `b`
- expected logical bytes: 10,100
- private flag: true
- tracker tier 0: `https://one.example/announce`
- tracker tier 1: `https://two.example/announce`
- URL seed: `https://seed.example/payload/`

Expected identities:

| Fixture | Format | V1 info hash | V2 info hash | Raw SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `create-matrix-v1.torrent` | V1 | `cf932f2cdf1fb5bf357dbd4c1c97c95fbc96b07d` | - | `8121988b62ae807f4dfe6344fa3538f1ab68e973af355f4d1ac21db21d730f2d` |
| `create-matrix-v2.torrent` | V2 | - | `974c6e1d173260e47ae5f979ba8705562ef41b49e0062fc93c2613be15dccf68` | `a34ad7c18fe97091228577ab79fd968da0457a2eedbe5657194a10e3fb1449cd` |
| `create-matrix-hybrid.torrent` | Hybrid | `b3646b48e0ecbf9034dc1bfc2955e8122902799b` | `5d31bb65bbbcaf2fdd841b4937bc1e0c6fcd5dfa90087e233cb4f5c167075310` | `2ef86e72e2e731c191f1a1cc9ec7912ddc53751cf41a5129c176d93fa7ef596a` |

The integration test requires byte-for-byte create parity, strict Domain reread, and a successful
public `TorrentEngine::verify()` recheck for every format.

## `file-order-policy/`

This bundle freezes the four `FileOrderPolicy` values across V1, V2 and Hybrid. Its Core-backed
generator creates a payload with root-level numeric names, a nested regular file and an empty file,
then writes all twelve torrent outputs. The integration matrix recreates that payload and requires
byte-for-byte equality with every fixture.

- payload logical bytes: 27,000; fixed piece length: 16 KiB
- `Lexicographical`, `CanonicalAlignment`, `Natural` and `BreadthFirst` each have V1/V2/Hybrid
  outputs
- V1 retains policy-specific ordering and info hashes; V2 and Hybrid converge to libtorrent's BEP
  52 canonical layout, so their canonical raw bytes and V2 info hashes are policy-independent
- the separate runtime symlink matrix covers all twelve policy/format combinations with a BEP 47
  link, while this fixture bundle remains regular-file-only for portable qBittorrent recheck

`CanonicalAlignment` V2 and Hybrid fixtures were force-rechecked to 100% by qBittorrent 4.6.3;
their exact hashes, state and dependency versions are recorded in `file-order-policy/provenance.env`.
The two manifests protect the torrent/provenance bundle and its payload independently.

Regenerate the bundle only with the pinned Core dependency graph:

```sh
cmake --build out/build/linux-clang-debug --target torrentutils_generate_file_order_policy_matrix
out/build/linux-clang-debug/tests/torrentutils_generate_file_order_policy_matrix \
  tests/fixtures/torrent-engine/file-order-policy
```

## `qbittorrent-followed-symlink/`

This curated fixture replaces the earlier unbounded Hybrid sample, which contained unrelated
directory names and lacked the payload and creation provenance needed for Exit-gate evidence.

- creator field: `qBittorrent v4.6.3`
- source content root: `DevBase` (stored as `payload/sample-content/`)
- piece length policy: fixed 32 KiB
- private flag: false
- trackers and web seeds: none
- recorded link: `links/alias.bin -> ../data/target.bin`
- qBittorrent recheck: 100% completed for V1, V2, and Hybrid

| Fixture | Format | Raw SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `qbittorrent-4.6.3-v1-followed-symlink.torrent` | V1 | `08e863db4a6128106fd6bc75268201362a765fdb369a2dd3b1ece1732419fff9` |
| `qbittorrent-4.6.3-v2-followed-symlink.torrent` | V2 | `4d91727d039ee9dd859abd5e09457c4eb86281c7d97a2f23a2b3bfde70765a7e` |
| `qbittorrent-4.6.3-hybrid-followed-symlink.torrent` | Hybrid | `c7468dae2a564d81c7d8c4ce26572d685204c85412016ea279e9785078bf2faf` |

Strict decoding exposes no file with the BEP 47 `l` attribute and no `symlink path`; each torrent
therefore records qBittorrent's historical ordinary followed-payload behavior rather than a
canonical BEP 47 symlink entry.

The versioned payload retains the actual relative symlink, its target bytes, and the independent
`symlinks.tsv` record. For portable Core verification, the integration test materializes the alias
as an ordinary file containing the recorded target bytes, matching the identity encoded by these
torrents while still preserving the original qBittorrent symlink evidence.

The nested `SHA256SUMS` and `payload-SHA256SUMS` use relocation-safe relative paths and cover the
payload, link, torrents, inspection reports, symlink record, and `provenance.env`. The originating
environment is recorded without host-identifying data:

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS; kernel: Linux 6.8.0-137-generic x86_64 GNU/Linux.
- filesystem: tmpfs, 4096-byte blocks; mount options: `tmpfs rw,noatime,inode64`.

## `retained-hybrid-padding.torrent`

- format: Hybrid
- piece length: 16 KiB
- payload root: `payload/`
- `a.bin`: 10,000 bytes, all ASCII `a`
- `b.bin`: 100 bytes, all ASCII `b`
- expected logical bytes: 10,100
- V1 info hash: `527f44dac29d48ca711879b9c6f7e117e539c08c`
- V2 info hash: `99f1d3786e2e7b47c96eed3eeaf7b10264ef4df88d174bd1b5f6a67d255e7512`
- raw torrent SHA-256:
  `63c6ba9bd26f2573dee05973220f7ace63bb181162067f8d00f566012d68375f`
- expected V1 alignment padding: 6,384 bytes after `a.bin` and 16,284 bytes after `b.bin`
- generator: `generate_retained_hybrid_padding.cpp`
- backend: libtorrent 2.0.14 from the locked vcpkg dependency graph

The generator is intentionally not part of the normal test build. To refresh the fixture, compile
it against the locked Debug dependency tree, pass the desired torrent path and a disposable work
directory, then run the full Torrent Engine tests. A refresh requires reviewing the raw torrent
bytes and all expected hashes before committing the replacement.

The verification test recreates only the two logical payload files. Padding entries must remain
virtual and must not appear in `VerificationReport` or verification-progress file snapshots.
